## Website design guides by industry

- [Website design for Gyms & Fitness Centres](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/gyms-and-fitness-centres/): A gym website has one job: turn a curious visitor into a free-trial booking. People choose a gym by location, price and the trainers they will meet, so your site should show all three in the first scroll and make enquiring one tap away.
- [Website design for Clinics & Healthcare](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/clinics/): Patients search for a clinic when they are worried, often late in the evening and on a phone. A clinic website should answer three questions quickly: who will see me, what do you treat and how do I get an appointment.
- [Website design for Dental Clinics](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/dental-clinics/): People searching for a dentist usually have a specific problem such as a toothache, braces or a missing tooth, and they compare cost and comfort before booking. A good dental website answers those two worries and makes the first appointment easy.
- [Website design for Tuition Centres](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/tuition-centres/): Parents choose a tuition centre by results, teachers and trust, and they usually decide after a conversation. Your website should give them the facts upfront and make booking a demo class as easy as sending a message.
- [Website design for Restaurants & Cafés](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/restaurants-and-cafes/): Diners decide in seconds, usually on a phone and often while standing outside. Your restaurant website should show what you are known for, the prices and how to reserve or order, before they scroll twice.
- [Website design for Beauty Parlours & Salons](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/beauty-parlours-and-salons/): Clients pick a parlour by the look of the work and how easy it is to book. A beauty website should show your best results, list services with prices and let a client request a slot in a minute, especially before weddings and festivals.
- [Website design for Homestays & Resorts](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/homestays-and-resorts/): Travellers compare many stays and book through platforms that charge commission. Your own website lets you show rooms honestly, offer a direct-booking benefit and answer the questions that decide a booking: location, food, access and price.
- [Website design for Crane & Heavy Equipment Services](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/crane-services/): Contractors and factories need a crane quickly and judge a supplier by capacity, safety and how fast they respond. A crane service website should list the fleet, show proof of safety and make requesting a quote a two-minute task.
- [Website design for Real Estate Agents](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/real-estate-agents/): Property buyers search by area and budget and trust agents who show real listings with clear details. A real estate website should present each property with photos, price and location, and make booking a site visit simple.
- [Website design for Landscaping Companies](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/landscaping-companies/): Garden customers buy with their eyes. A landscaping website should show finished gardens first, explain what you design and build, and make a free site visit easy to book.
- [Website design for Cleaning Services](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/cleaning-services/): Customers hire cleaners when they are busy or about to host, and they worry about trust and price. A cleaning company website should show fixed prices, who will come to the home and how to book a slot in a minute.
- [Website design for Auditoriums & Event Venues](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/auditoriums-and-event-venues/): Event organisers shortlist venues by capacity, date availability and what is included. An auditorium website should state seating clearly, show the hall honestly and make checking a date a one-tap enquiry.
- [Website design for Interior Designers](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/interior-designers/): Homeowners choose an interior designer by portfolio, process and trust, and a bad experience is a big risk for them. Your website should show finished homes, explain how a project runs and reduce uncertainty about cost and timelines.
- [Website design for Photographers & Studios](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/photographers/): Photographers are chosen on the quality of their work and how easy they are to book for a specific date. A photography website should let the portfolio carry the first impression, then answer price, availability and delivery questions.
- [Website design for Wedding Planners](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/wedding-planners/): Couples and families entrust a wedding planner with the biggest event of their lives, so trust and clarity matter more than anything. Your website should show real events, explain how planning works and make a first conversation easy.
- [Website design for Car Detailing Studios & Garages](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/car-detailing-and-garages/): Car owners trust a detailer with an expensive asset and look for proof of quality, honest advice and convenience. A car care website should show results, explain each service in plain language and make booking and pickup easy.
- [Website design for Pest Control Companies](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/pest-control-companies/): Customers search for pest control when they already have a problem, often urgently. A pest control website should reassure them about safety, explain the treatment and offer a fast way to book an inspection.
- [Website design for Yoga Studios & Wellness Centres](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/yoga-studios/): People looking for yoga want a calm space, a teacher they trust and times that fit their day. A yoga studio website should communicate that atmosphere, show the schedule clearly and make the first class easy to book.
- [Website design for Chartered Accountants & Tax Consultants](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/chartered-accountants/): Business owners look for an accountant they can trust with money and compliance. A CA firm website should explain services in plain language, set expectations on documents and fees and let a prospect request a consultation.
- [Website design for Pet Care & Grooming](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/pet-care-and-grooming/): Pet owners treat their animals as family and choose a service they trust with them. A pet care website should show gentle handling, clean spaces and clear prices, and make booking grooming or boarding simple.
- [Website design for Solar Installers](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/solar-installers/): Homeowners and businesses research solar carefully because it is a large, long-term purchase. A solar installer website should explain system sizes and savings honestly, address subsidy and net metering questions and make a free site survey easy to book.
- [Website design for Jewellery Shops](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/jewellery-shops/): Jewellery buyers care about trust, purity and price transparency before they care about design. A jewellery shop website should show collections beautifully, explain purity and making charges clearly and invite shoppers to visit.
- [Website design for Travel Agencies & Tour Operators](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/travel-agencies/): Travellers compare many agents and choose the one that feels reliable and explains the trip clearly. A travel agency website should present itineraries with prices and inclusions, and let people ask about their dates quickly.
- [Website design for Manufacturers & Industrial Suppliers](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/manufacturers/): Industrial buyers look for capability, quality and reliability before price, and they often send enquiries with drawings. A manufacturer's website should list capabilities and tolerances, show proof of quality and make a quote request detailed but simple.
- [Website design for Software & IT Companies](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/software-companies/): Clients hire a software partner on evidence: past work, clear process and communication. A software company website should explain services in business terms, show case studies and make a first discussion easy to schedule.
- [Website design for Fashion Boutiques](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/fashion-boutiques/): Fashion shoppers respond to visuals and convenience. A boutique website should present collections in a clean lookbook, explain tailoring and alterations and let shoppers ask about a piece with one tap.
- [Website design for Online Stores & Product Sellers](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/online-stores/): Online shoppers need to trust a seller they have not met. A small online store should show products clearly, explain delivery and returns honestly and make ordering simple, even if orders begin on WhatsApp.
- [Website design for B2B & Corporate Service Providers](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/b2b-and-corporate-services/): Business buyers research suppliers before they ever call, and they look for clarity on what you do, who you serve and how you work. A B2B company website should explain services plainly, show experience and invite a proposal request.
- [Website design for Insurance & Finance Advisors](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/insurance-and-finance-advisors/): People approach an insurance or finance advisor for peace of mind, so trust and clarity come before products. An advisor's website should explain options in plain language, show credentials and make a free review easy to request.
- [Website design for Law Firms & Advocates](https://demo.qrenzy.com/websites-for/law-firms-and-advocates/): People looking for a lawyer are often anxious and want clarity and discretion. A law firm's website should present practice areas and advocates professionally, offer informational guidance and provide a discreet way to ask for a consultation, within the rules that govern advocates.
